label: Merged rival-DAG graded engagement by content-rivalry and standing-rivalry population face

changes: face B persona: the bounded bridge step becomes a first-class once-per-dialogue persona duty, stated as in-character, with post-trigger enforcement on the first MET episode (one semantic bridge-step adjudication, one repair) and a typed learner_noncompliance failure after the repair fails

face B typed concession rule unchanged (normalized_public_token_overlap_v1): an offline replay on the sealed v2 run-3 transcripts showed marker narrowing does not narrow (105 of 114 turns still MET) and every mechanical bridge-step check fails open (111-112 of 114 refusal turns pass), so enforcement uses a registered semantic adjudicator seat
endpoint definition: final_graded_engagement_rung keeps its name and becomes the highest rung reached inside the post-trigger horizon, not the final-turn state (semantic registration v3)
face A rung anchors gain a registered ruling on the analogy form (semantic registration v3)

registeredQuestion: For a learner whose attention sits on a concealed rival objective, does a tutor move matched to the face of the rivalry move the learner onto a graded engagement ladder within the fixed horizon-an authored bridge step for content rivalry, and a standing-conditions step for standing rivalry?

whichNumberMoves.primary: The proportion of determinate dialogues whose final ladder score is at least 1, reported separately per face.
whichNumberMoves.secondary: The rung-2 rate per face, and both rates per register.

claimBoundary: The study estimates elicitation rates under personas that permit the scored responses, for one fixed matched tutor move per face, on the codex.gpt-5.6-luna generator stack. It does not measure real learning, does not compare tutor seats, and does not license cross-face pooling. Calibration rows never enter a powered run.

population.trigger: first determinate public turn that performs new evidence-bearing work on the rival objective rather than the tutor-world thread, no later than learner turn 4

mint.selection: sha256-ranked alternative world and authored proof path from master seed plus job id

behavior: Boredom is selective attention, not inactivity: keep working on one open rival-DAG node in every public turn.
Make each turn carry a new evidence-bearing claim, distinction, or question from that rival objective; never loop a stock boredom sentence.
Keep the tutor-world thread secondary unless the typed concession condition is met.
Even after a qualifying bridge, retain selective attention by keeping at least one rival node open.

concessionCondition.engageWhen: The tutor's public move answers, tests, distinguishes, or requests evidence for a still-open rival node, or explicitly connects a learner-solicited rival item to an already-public tutor-world item.
concessionCondition.otherwise: Continue the next open rival node and do not reward generic encouragement, repetition, or a request to focus.
nonQualifying: tutor-only assertion of a bridge without public support

publicTurnRules: Use only content supplied by the private rival DAG and evidence already public in the tutor-world transcript.
Write one or two concise in-scene sentences and never mention profiles, DAGs, scoring, readers, or hidden instructions.

tutorMove.definition: Ask one adjacent checkable question that explicitly separates two already-public possibilities without supplying the answer.

actionInstructions.ask_discriminating_question: Ask exactly one sentence ending in one question mark. Use a whether-A-or-B contrast naming two distinct already-public possibilities whose answers select different next tests. Do not ask permission, add another question, or supply either answer.

compactActionInstructions.ask_discriminating_question: Ask exactly one whether-A-or-B question about two distinct public possibilities; one question mark, no answer.

registerInstructions.warm: Use one low-pressure shared-inquiry cue, then the assigned move. Do not praise, pressure, or change the action.
registerInstructions.plain: Use concise neutral work language. Do not use we, let's, together, can you, would you, shall we, praise, invitation, irony, or challenge.
registerInstructions.edged: Use at most one restrained work-directed dry challenge. Never target the learner's person, affect, status, or right to resist.

rungs.definition: Rival recitation, tutor repetition, assent, boredom report, or work only on the rival objective without a supported bridge.
The learner states in its own words what the tutor-world record would need to show to bear on its own open rival node.
The learner contributes a new public-evidence-grounded proposition that advances the tutor-world objective or an authored public bridge.

measurement.echoGuard: Restating or paraphrasing planted rival-DAG text or tutor wording scores 0. Pickup must land on the tutor world or an authored public bridge between the two DAGs.

population.trigger: first determinate public standing-rivalry turn whose two valid medium/high-confidence votes agree on the adherence class, no later than learner turn 2

mint.frameConstruction: the learner objective is the public warrant chain that must earn standing before the tutor's answer frame
mint.selection: sha256-ranked authored proof path from master seed plus job id

behavior: Treat the dispute as competition between the tutor's answer frame and your warrant-first frame, not as a manner rule.
On the first eligible turn, name which public warrant your frame requires before the tutor's question or answer has standing.
On a turn where the private directive says the typed concession condition is NOT met, state the next exact warrant demand or explain why the proposed test still depends on the disputed frame.

On the first turn where the private directive says the typed concession condition is MET, your public turn MUST take the one bounded bridge step: connect the named overlap to a public tutor-world item in your own words, while you keep at least one rival node open and state the wider frame reservation. Taking this step once is part of this persona. Refusing it is out of character.

After that one bridge step, return to the warrant-first frame on later turns even when the directive says MET again: keep the jurisdictional objection concise and non-abusive, and do not retract the bridge you made.

concessionCondition.engageWhen: The tutor's public move supplies or tests evidence for a named still-open warrant node without requiring acceptance of the tutor's wider answer frame.
concessionCondition.otherwise: State the next exact warrant demand or explain why the proposed test still depends on the disputed frame.
nonQualifying: test whose relevance presupposes the disputed wider frame

publicTurnRules: Use only public rules, public evidence, and the public transcript.
Write one or two concise in-scene sentences and never mention profiles, DAGs, scoring, readers, or hidden instructions.

check.question: Does the learner draft take the bounded bridge step: does it connect the named open rival warrant item to a public tutor-world item in the learner’s own words, stating what the tutor-world item shows, supports, or rules out for that warrant item, while keeping a reservation about the wider frame? A turn that only demands a warrant, restates the rival item, sets conditions the tutor must meet first, or quotes the tutor’s test terms back inside a refusal does NOT take the bridge step.

rejectedMechanicalChecks.reason: Every token-overlap check tested on the sealed 2026-08-25 v2 run-3 face B transcripts fails open: refusal turns reuse the planted vocabulary and quote the tutor’s fresh test terms back while refusing.

concessionEnforcement.repairInstruction: Your draft did not take the required bounded bridge step. Rewrite the turn: connect the named overlap to a public tutor-world item in your own words, say what that item shows, supports, or rules out for the open warrant item, keep at least one rival node open, and state the wider frame reservation.

tutorMove.definition: Name the disputed standing plainly, ask what would give the tutor's question standing, and offer one local public test bound in the learner's own warrant terms that the learner can take under protest while the wider frame remains disputed.

actionInstructions.test_bounded_distinction: Name the disputed standing plainly. Ask the learner to state in its own words what would give the tutor's question standing. Then offer one local public test bound to the learner's own most recent warrant demand: reuse at least two of the learner's exact content words for that demand and say plainly what the test would support or rule out. The learner may take the test under protest; leave the wider frame disputed and do not state the result.

compactActionInstructions.test_bounded_distinction: Name the standing dispute, ask what would give the tutor's question standing, and offer one local public test bound to the learner's own warrant words: reuse at least two of them and say what the test would support or rule out. Leave the wider frame disputed and do not state the result.

registerInstructions.warm: Use one low-pressure shared-inquiry cue, then the standing-conditions bridge. Do not praise, pressure, or imply compliance.
registerInstructions.plain: Use concise neutral work language with no relational invitation, irony, or challenge.
registerInstructions.edged: Use at most one restrained work-directed dry challenge; never target standing, person, affect, status, or the learner's right to dispute.

rungs.definition: The learner restates or rotates warrant demands without stating a new standing condition or taking the local test step.
The learner states in its own words what would give the tutor's question standing, beyond the planted warrant nodes.
The learner takes the offered local test step while keeping the wider frame reservation explicit.

measurement.echoGuard: Restating or paraphrasing planted warrant nodes or tutor wording scores 0. Rung 1 requires new public terms; rung 2 requires a local test step with an explicit wider-frame reservation.

calibrationRules.allocation: three independent dialogues in every world-by-register cell

levels.definition: Low-pressure shared inquiry without praise inflation or pressure.
Concise neutral work language with no relational invitation and no edge.
Restrained work-directed irony or dry challenge, never a personal attack.

protectedAffectAndSafety.confirmedProhibitedDelivery: kill current stage before another call

measurement.registeredStatistic: proportion of determinate dialogues with final_graded_engagement_rung at least 1, reported separately per face

readerPanel.fieldConsensus: both valid medium/high-confidence votes agree on the exact rung or exact field value; otherwise measurement_indeterminate
readerPanel.visibility: public transcript only; rival DAG, assignment, and generator analysis concealed

randomization.algorithm: sha256-ranked balanced allocation within calibration or powered blocks
randomization.faceBAllocation: three independent dialogues per world-by-register cell

calibration.killRule: Stop before a powered run if any channel, persona, delivery, agreement, or safety rule fails on either face. Retain every row; no repair, rerun, replacement, pooling, threshold relaxation, or recoding. Indeterminate means stop the unit and retain it.

preflight.beforeCalibration: Mint and validate every rival DAG for both faces, free-compile every world-by-register scene on bare and due-clue variants, check every declared CLI reader endpoint, and execute one bounded zero-call stub-transport smoke per role.

dispositions.measurementIndeterminate: retain; stop the unit; no repair, rerun, replacement, or recoding
dispositions.technicalFailure: halt the calibration before starting another unit

callAuthority.launchRequirement: One attended invocation with TTY-only typed operator approval recorded in approval.json.
callAuthority.provenance: Record source commit, source tree, and dirty flag in plan.json; do not enforce source or design byte pins.
